newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian Minister says alcohol quota could be cut.
newsitem.headline: Russian Minister says alcohol quota could be cut.

text.p: The Russian government may rescind in the next few days a quota on imported alcohol planned to come into effect on January 1, Foreign Economic Relations Minister Oleg Davydov said on Monday.
Licencing would replace quotas and government quality control efforts would be increased, Prime-Tass news agency quoted him as telling a news conference.

"Such a decision is directly related to the meeting of the Temporary Emergency (tax) Commission meeting last week, at which the institution of a state monopoly on the alcohol market was announced," he said.
President Boris Yeltsin chaired the meeting of the special tax committee last week and his chief of staff Anatoly Chubais later said that the state would clamp down on production and sale of alcohol.
Davydov said: "This changes the heart of the matter, as it is a stronger measure than putting quotas on spirits."
